# GPU work runs in its own thread so that receiving/concatenating frames overlaps inference
    infer_q = queue.Queue(maxsize=3)
    done_q = queue.Queue()
    inflight = [0]

    def infer_loop():
        nonlocal t_gpu
        while True:
            job = infer_q.get()
            if job is None:
                break
            items, x = job
            t0 = time.time()
            try:
                counts = det(x).numpy()
            except Exception as e:  # never lose the bookkeeping, even on a GPU error
                print(f"[run] inference error: {e}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
                counts = np.zeros((len(x), 5), np.int32)
            t_gpu += time.time() - t0
            done_q.put((items, counts))

    it = threading.Thread(target=infer_loop, daemon=True)
    it.start()

attachment.snippet:
13	```bash
14	python3.11 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
15	```
16	
17	```bash
18	pip install -r requirements.txt
19	```
20	
21	`torch==2.7.1` from PyPI ships CUDA 12.6 runtime libraries and `tensorrt-cu12` ships TensorRT 10.13,
22	so only the NVIDIA driver is needed from the system.
23	
24	## Preparation command (run once, needs internet, not timed)
25	
26	```bash
27	python prepare.py
28	```
29	
30	This does three things:
31	- downloads the official `yolo11l.pt` into `weights/`;
32	- exports it to ONNX;
33	- builds a **TensorRT FP16 engine for the local GPU** (`weights/yolo11l_fp16.engine`, about
34	  5 minutes). The engine has a dynamic batch size of 1–32 and dynamic image sizes up to 640×640.
35	
36	If the engine build fails for any reason, `run.py` automatically uses the PyTorch FP16 model
37	instead. That is slower but gives the same results. `run.py` never needs the internet.
38	
39	## Run (offline)
40	
41	```bash
42	python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl
43	```
44	
45	Progress is printed to stderr every 30 s. Useful options (defaults are the submitted configuration):
46	
47	| option | meaning |
48	|---|---|
49	| `--fps-samples K` | frames analysed per second of video (`0` = every frame) |
50	| `--workers N` | decoder processes (default: CPU count − 2) |
51	| `--batch B` | GPU batch size (default 64) |
52	| `--no-trt` | ignore the TensorRT engine and use PyTorch FP16 |
53	| `--infer-threads T` | GPU inference threads, each with its own CUDA stream (default 2) |
54	| `--fp32` | PyTorch FP32 (slow; for checks) |
55	
56	## How it works
57	
58	1. **Reader thread.** Streams rows out of each Parquet file one at a time with `pyarrow` (`mp4`
59	   column only). The video id is `<file name>:<row>`.
60	2. **Decoder processes** (one video each, a pool sized to the CPU). Each video is decoded with
61	   PyAV/FFmpeg. Non-reference frames are skipped by the decoder (`skip_frame=NONREF`), but
62	   packet timestamps still give the true last second. Timestamps come from `pts` relative to the
63	   first decoded frame, and the display-matrix rotation tag is applied. Only **3 evenly spaced
64	   frames per second** are converted. swscale does the YUV→BGR conversion and the bilinear
65	   resize in one pass, and the frame is then padded like Ultralytics' `LetterBox` (rect mode,
66	   e.g. 384×640 for 16:9).
67	3. **Shared-memory hand-off.** Decoders write letterboxed uint8 frames into a ring of
68	   fixed-size slots in one `multiprocessing.shared_memory` block. Queues only carry slot numbers.
69	   The Parquet reader hands out the biggest videos of each file first, so long videos don't
70	   finish last.
71	4. **GPU.** Frames from different videos with the same shape are batched. Batches are split or
72	   padded to fixed sizes of 4, 8, 16 or 32, so cuDNN/TensorRT never retune for odd sizes. Two
73	   inference threads, each with its own CUDA stream, run YOLO11l (TensorRT FP16, or PyTorch FP16
74	   channels-last as the fallback).
75	   Post-processing stays on the GPU and mirrors Ultralytics: best class per box, conf > 0.4,

23	
24	## Preparation command (run once, needs internet, not timed)
25	
26	```bash

28	```
29	
30	This does three things:
31	- downloads the official `yolo11l.pt` into `weights/`;
32	- exports it to ONNX;
33	- builds a **TensorRT FP16 engine for the local GPU** (`weights/yolo11l_fp16.engine`, about
34	  5 minutes). The engine has a dynamic batch size of 1–32 and dynamic image sizes up to 640×640.
35	
36	If the engine build fails for any reason, `run.py` automatically uses the PyTorch FP16 model
37	instead. That is slower but gives the same results. `run.py` never needs the internet.
38	
39	## Run (offline)
40	
41	```bash
42	python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl
43	```
44	
45	Progress is printed to stderr every 30 s. Useful options (defaults are the submitted configuration):
46	
47	| option | meaning |
48	|---|---|
49	| `--fps-samples K` | frames analysed per second of video (`0` = every frame) |
50	| `--workers N` | decoder processes (default: CPU count − 2) |
51	| `--batch B` | GPU batch size (default 64) |
52	| `--no-trt` | ignore the TensorRT engine and use PyTorch FP16 |
53	| `--infer-threads T` | GPU inference threads, each with its own CUDA stream (default 2) |
54	| `--fp32` | PyTorch FP32 (slow; for checks) |
55	
56	## How it works
57	
58	1. **Reader thread.** Streams rows out of each Parquet file one at a time with `pyarrow` (`mp4`
59	   column only). The video id is `<file name>:<row>`.
60	2. **Decoder processes** (one video each, a pool sized to the CPU). Each video is decoded with
61	   PyAV/FFmpeg. Non-reference frames are skipped by the decoder (`skip_frame=NONREF`), but
62	   packet timestamps still give the true last second. Timestamps come from `pts` relative to the
63	   first decoded frame, and the display-matrix rotation tag is applied. Only **3 evenly spaced
64	   frames per second** are converted. swscale does the YUV→BGR conversion and the bilinear
65	   resize in one pass, and the frame is then padded like Ultralytics' `LetterBox` (rect mode,
66	   e.g. 384×640 for 16:9).
67	3. **Shared-memory hand-off.** Decoders write letterboxed uint8 frames into a ring of
68	   fixed-size slots in one `multiprocessing.shared_memory` block. Queues only carry slot numbers.
69	   The Parquet reader hands out the biggest videos of each file first, so long videos don't
70	   finish last.
71	4. **GPU.** Frames from different videos with the same shape are batched. Batches are split or
72	   padded to fixed sizes of 4, 8, 16 or 32, so cuDNN/TensorRT never retune for odd sizes. Two
73	   inference threads, each with its own CUDA stream, run YOLO11l (TensorRT FP16, or PyTorch FP16
74	   channels-last as the fallback).
75	   Post-processing stays on the GPU and mirrors Ultralytics: best class per box, conf > 0.4,

# Hardware used for the full 50-file run

**Where:** a rented cloud GPU on [Modal](https://modal.com). It was a serverless container started with
`modal_app.py` (`gpu="L40S", cpu=16, memory=65536`). The timed run had networking blocked, like the
graders' run.

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA L40S, 46 GB (46068 MiB), driver 620.70 |
| CPU | 16 vCPUs reserved. The CPU model is not exposed inside Modal's sandbox (`lscpu` shows "unknown"). |
| RAM | 64 GB limit for the container |
| Disk | Modal Volume (network-attached, SSD-backed) holding the 50 Parquet files (about 25 GB) |
| OS | Debian 12 (bookworm) container image, Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.7.1 + CUDA 12.6, TensorRT 10.13 |

## Full-run time (start to finish)

The final version took **906 s (15 min 6 s)** for all 50 files:
- 1,650 videos;
- 461,757 output lines;
- 1,344,118 frames analysed;
- 0 errors.

It was run with:

```bash
python run.py --input /data/finevideo/data --output results.jsonl
```

The TensorRT engine was built beforehand by `prepare.py`, which is untimed.

Other full-run times on the same machine:

| version | full 50 files |
|---|---|
| PyTorch FP16 (no TensorRT), shared-memory ring buffer | 1,574 s |
| TensorRT FP16, one inference thread | 960 s |
| **final: TensorRT FP16, 2 inference threads, pinned staging buffers** | **906 s** |
